'''Yohashira Shrine''' (四柱神社, Yohashira Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ōte|ja|大手 (松本市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōte, Matsumoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11435537}}, Matsumoto City, Nagano Prefecture. Locally, it is often referred to as "Shintō-san" due to the Shintō festival held in October. It is also commonly misread as "Shihashira."

== Overview ==
[[File:Yohashira jinja01s1920.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Shrine grounds]]
The shrine's name derives from its enshrinement of four deities: {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}, {{ill|Takamimusubi|ja|高皇産霊神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamimusubi|qid=Q125400}}, {{ill|Kamimusubi|ja|神皇産霊神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamimusubi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミムスビ}}, and {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}.

{{nihongo|Hashira|柱|lit pillar}} is the counter for gods in Japanese<ref>https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9F%B1</ref>

The shrine originated from the Shinto {{ill|Taikyo Institute|ja|中教院|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūkyōin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大教院|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11435598}} established in Matsumoto, {{ill|Chikuma Prefecture|ja|筑摩県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Prefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11602831}}, in 1872 (Meiji 5). The Chūkyōin began enshrining the four deities in 1874 (Meiji 7). In 1879 (Meiji 12), the shrine was moved to its current location, and a shrine building was constructed, formally establishing Yohashira Shrine as a village shrine. The shrine building was destroyed in the Matsumoto Great Fire of 1888 (Meiji 21) and was rebuilt in 1924 (Taishō 13). In 1959 (Shōwa 34), Yohashira Shrine was listed as a Beppyo Shrine.

== Transportation Access ==
* 10-minute walk from {{ill|Matsumoto Station|en|Matsumoto Station|qid=Q843167|lt=Matsumoto Station}} on the {{ill|Japan Railways Group|en|Japan Railways Group|qid=Q864495|lt=JR}} line
* Alipico Transportation (commonly known as Matsumoto Electric Railway Bus), get off at Daimyōmachi bus stop via Matsumoto Castle, and it is immediately nearby
